assets.description: After my bike wipeout, I'm on the side of the road letting the adreneline burn off. While I'm waiting, the FedEx truck gets hit by another truck. Right as I'm looking up from the highly interesting street sweeping (I just had a wreck, what can I say?), the two trucks tangle. Watch closely or you might miss it. And then the stream of peds to see what happened. The FedEx truck, being parked on the curb, was angled into the street. When the other truck went to pass, the driver didn't pull around far enough to prevent the tops of the trucks colliding with each other.

assets.creator: The Scan Man Gallery
assets.action_hint: vintage ice and snow daredevil stunts and crashes
assets.credit: YouTube : Daredevils On Ice (1945) - 16mm - Silent with Sound - HD – View/save archived versions on archive.org
assets.categories: Films in the public domain|English-language films|PD US not renewed|Videos from YouTube|Videos of 1945|Uploaded with video2commons|1945 films of the United States|Transitional sound films|PD-US missing SDC copyright status|Black-and-white films of the United States
assets.description: A friend handed me a bag with films in it and said "If you want to scan these, I'd like to know what is on them". Being curious as well, I started doing just that. This is a Castle Films "Sports" film showing various Ice and Snow sports. This film was sold two ways, as a silent film and a sound film (in 16mm only). In 1945 there were still older 16mm projectors that didn't have sound and had sproket holes on both sides of the film. So sound films would be damaged if run through them. Producing both gave Castle a bigger market. I found another version of this film with sound and edited in the soundtrack. It had to be re-timed a bit because the other film was running fast (we're locked at 24FPS with our scanning method). I think it's fun and you get to see the Intertitles from the silent version as well. Enjoy.

assets.description: Staff Sgt. Carl Clegg, a Newberry, South Carolina native, adds a little challenging fun into his training plan this week with a #TrickShotTuesday. This U.S. Army Marksmanship Unit Service Pistol Team Soldier regularly competes in bullseye competitions that require shooting with one hand. The ability to consistently and accurately hit the target in this shooting sports discipline is no easy task. So, USAMU Soldiers typically train at tasks that have added challenges, which has proven to increase their success rates in competition. In this shot, Clegg trains by attempting to shoot a playing card in half. That's down the thin side of the card, not the face. Check out how well he does.
